config.title: Photo Capture & Upload

intro.title: Photo Capture & Upload
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a mobile app that can take photos using the device's camera and upload them to a server. You will learn how to use the Capacitor Camera API to capture images and the Capacitor Filesystem API to read the photo data. The core programming concept involves using Promises to handle asynchronous operations like camera access and file reading. You will implement this in an Ionic Angular app, creating a service to manage the photo logic and a component with a button to trigger the capture and upload process.
intro.usecase: Photo capture and upload functionality is essential in mobile apps that require user-generated content, such as social media platforms like Instagram or Facebook where users post photos. In e-commerce apps like eBay or Facebook Marketplace, sellers use this feature to upload product images directly from their device camera. Customer service applications often allow users to attach photos of issues or documents for verification purposes. Healthcare apps might use photo capture for telemedicine consultations where patients share symptoms visually. Even note-taking apps like Evernote use this pattern to let users add photos to their notes for richer documentation.

objectives: Import the Camera plugin from @capacitor/camera to access device camera functionality.
Define a method to capture a photo using the Camera.getPhoto() method with specified options.
Implement error handling to catch and display camera operation failures.
Construct an interface to store captured photo data including webPath and format.
Use Angular's HttpClient to send HTTP POST requests to an upload endpoint.
Apply FormData to package captured photo files for multipart/form-data uploads.
Execute conditional logic to check camera permissions before attempting capture.
Control UI state with loading indicators during photo capture and upload operations.
Store captured photo references in component state for display and reuse.
Retrieve and display uploaded photo URLs from server responses.
Modify camera options to configure quality, allowEditing, and resultType parameters.
Invoke the upload method automatically after successful photo capture.

steps.title: Create the PhotoCaptureComponent
steps.instruction: Create a new Angular component class named PhotoCaptureComponent. Use the @Component decorator with the configuration: standalone: true, and an imports array containing the Ionic components you imported earlier.
steps.hint: Start with 'export class PhotoCaptureComponent {}' and add the @Component decorator above it. The decorator should have a selector, standalone: true, and imports: [IonButton, IonContent, IonHeader, IonTitle, IonToolbar].
steps.expectedOutcome: A PhotoCaptureComponent class is defined with the @Component decorator configured as a standalone component.
successCriteria: The code should include: 1) @Component decorator with selector, standalone: true, and imports array, 2) export class PhotoCaptureComponent {}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the PhotoCaptureComponent as a standalone Angular component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you include the @Component decorator with standalone: true and the imports array?
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Make sure to use the @Component decorator and export the class.

steps.hint: Set the template property to a string containing the HTML structure with the Ionic components you imported.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of a component template with Ionic structure
template: `
  <ion-header>
    <ion-toolbar>
      <ion-title>My App</ion-title>
    </ion-toolbar>
  </ion-header>
  <ion-content>
    <!-- Content will go here -->
  </ion-content>
`
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a basic Ionic page structure defined in its template, ready for adding content and functionality.
successCriteria: The template property should be defined with IonHeader, IonToolbar, IonTitle, and IonContent components in a valid HTML structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the component template with the basic Ionic page structure. This provides the visual foundation for your photo capture app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the template might be missing some required Ionic components or the structure isn't quite complete. Make sure you have IonHeader, IonToolbar, IonTitle, and IonContent all included.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure doesn't match what's needed. Remember to define the template property with IonHeader, IonToolbar, IonTitle, and IonContent components in a proper HTML structure.

steps.title: Initialize photo state property
steps.instruction: Inside the PhotoCaptureComponent class, add a property named 'photo' with type 'string | undefined' to store the captured photo data URL. Initialize it as undefined.
steps.hint: Add a class property declaration with the appropriate TypeScript type annotation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a typed property to store captured photo data.
successCriteria: The PhotoCaptureComponent class should contain a property named 'photo' with type 'string | undefined' initialized to undefined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a typed property to store photo data. This will be essential for displaying captured images.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a property named 'photo' with the correct type 'string | undefined' and initialized it to undefined.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't yet have the required property. Add a property named 'photo' with type 'string | undefined' and initialize it to undefined inside the PhotoCaptureComponent class.

steps.expectedOutcome: The template will have a button with 'Take Photo' text inside the content area.
successCriteria: The template contains an IonButton element with 'Take Photo' text inside the IonContent.

steps.title: Define capturePhoto method
steps.instruction: In the PhotoCaptureComponent class, create an async method named capturePhoto that will handle photo capture.
steps.hint: Add a method inside the class using the async keyword and the method name capturePhoto.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class now has an empty async capturePhoto method ready for implementation.
successCriteria: The method must be named capturePhoto, be async, and be defined inside the PhotoCaptureComponent class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the capturePhoto method. This gives us a place to implement the photo capture logic in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the method is named exactly 'capturePhoto', uses the async keyword, and is defined inside the PhotoCaptureComponent class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The capturePhoto method wasn't properly defined. Check that you're adding an async method with the correct name inside the component class.

steps.title: Store captured photo data
steps.instruction: Inside the capturePhoto method, assign the dataUrl from the photo result to the component's photo property.
steps.hint: The Camera plugin returns a photo object with a dataUrl property. Use this.dataUrl = photo.dataUrl to store it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The capturePhoto method now stores the photo's dataUrl in the component's photo property.
successCriteria: The capturePhoto method must assign photo.dataUrl to this.photo.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully stored the captured photo data in the component's state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're assigning the dataUrl property from the photo result to the component's photo property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The photo data isn't being stored correctly. Check that you're assigning photo.dataUrl to this.photo inside the capturePhoto method.

steps.title: Add photo display area
steps.instruction: Add IonGrid, IonRow, and IonCol components below the capture button in the template to create a grid layout for displaying the captured photo.
steps.hint: Import the grid components from '@ionic/angular/standalone' and add them to your template after the button.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding grid components to an Ionic Angular template
<IonGrid>
  <IonRow>
    <IonCol>
      <!-- Content goes here -->
    </IonCol>
  </IonRow>
</IonGrid>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will have a grid structure ready to display the captured photo, but the photo won't be shown yet.
successCriteria: IonGrid, IonRow, and IonCol components are added to the template after the button comment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the grid components to create a layout for displaying photos.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some grid components, but make sure to include all three: IonGrid, IonRow, and IonCol.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid components weren't added correctly. Check that you've imported IonGrid, IonRow, and IonCol and added them to the template.

steps.title: Display captured photo
steps.instruction: Inside the IonCol component in your template, add an IonImg component that displays the captured photo. Use Angular's *ngIf directive to only show the image when the 'photo' property has a value, and bind its 'src' attribute to the 'photo' property.
steps.hint: Use <IonImg *ngIf="photo" [src]="photo"></IonImg> inside the IonCol. Remember to import IonImg if needed.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include an IonImg component that conditionally displays the captured photo when the 'photo' property has a value.
successCriteria: Add an IonImg element inside the IonCol with *ngIf="photo" and [src]="photo" attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added conditional rendering for the captured photo using Ionic's IonImg component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both the *ngIf directive and the [src] binding to the IonImg element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The IonImg component isn't properly configured. Check that it has *ngIf="photo" and [src]="photo" attributes inside the IonCol.

steps.title: Add upload button
steps.instruction: Add a second IonButton component below the photo display grid in your template. The button should have the text 'Upload Photo' and be wired to an uploadPhoto method using Angular's event binding syntax.
steps.hint: Use the IonButton component with (click) event binding. Place it after the IonGrid closing tag.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Inside an Angular template -->
<IonButton expand="block" (click)="uploadPhoto()">Upload Photo</IonButton>
steps.expectedOutcome: A second button labeled 'Upload Photo' appears below the photo grid, ready to trigger an upload action.
successCriteria: The template contains an IonButton with text 'Upload Photo' and (click)="uploadPhoto()" event binding, placed after the IonGrid.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the upload button to the UI. The button is now ready to trigger the upload functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it might be missing the correct text, event binding, or placement. Make sure it's an IonButton with 'Upload Photo' text, (click)="uploadPhoto()", and placed after the IonGrid.
steps.feedbackWrong: The upload button is not correctly implemented. Check that you've added an IonButton component with the proper text and event binding syntax.
